name: MetaX MetaXLink (multi-GPU interconnect)
bandwidth_basis: NULL - deliberately, and this record exists to CLOSE A DOCUMENTED NEGATIVE RATHER THAN TO ASSERT ANYTHING. The prior audit pass of this slice recorded that 'metaxlink' had no sourceable record; this pass confirms that negative still holds after a wider search, and the search result itself is the finding. The ONLY source this repo holds on MetaX is cn-metax-wikipedia, a SECONDARY aggregator (kind 'review') whose underlying citations are DIGITIMES (Li, 2025-01-22 and Liang, 2025-04-10) and IT Home - and that source states plainly that it carries 'multi-GPU interconnect' as a bare capability phrase for the MXC500, with NO rate, NO port count, NO link count, NO topology and NO direction convention. MetaX's own product pages carry no interconnect specification. Per this repo's contract a wrong confident record is worse than an open question, so every rate field is null and the capability is recorded in topology instead. TO RESOLVE: find a MetaX MXC500 or MACA product datasheet, or MetaX's own developer documentation, stating MetaXLink's per-link rate and direction convention. Until then this record must not be cited by any benchmark, gotcha or decision table - and specifically, it is excluded from the B* table in docs/11-interconnect-decision.md, which can only be built on fabrics with a sourced per-direction rate.
topology: NOT PUBLISHED in any source this repo holds. What is recorded: the MXC500 (training/HPC, June 2023, MACA 2.0, 7 nm) is described as CUDA-compatible and as having a 'multi-GPU interconnect'; the N100 (inference, June 2023, HBM2E, 160 TOPS INT8 / 80 TFLOPS FP16) is the sibling inference part. No port count, no mesh or switch topology, and no statement of the maximum supported GPU count per domain.
switching: NOT PUBLISHED. No MetaX switch part is named in any source this repo holds.
notes: Added 2026-10-03 as the honest closure of a dangling reference: accelerators/metax-c500-n100 lists 'metaxlink' in its interconnect array and no record existed, so the reference could not be resolved. Unlike the two other dangling references closed in this same pass (huawei-ub-link, moore-threads-mtlink), this one CANNOT be filled with a number, and the difference is instructive. Huawei's Atlas pages and Moore Threads' S4000 page both publish an explicit rate for their proprietary fabrics, so those records carry sourced bandwidth. MetaX publishes nothing: the single source this repo holds is a Wikipedia page citing DIGITIMES, and it says only that a multi-GPU interconnect exists. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR A READER IS SPECIFIC: because there is no per-direction rate, MetaX cannot appear in the tensor-parallel crossover table in docs/11-interconnect-decision.md at all, and no B* can be computed for it. That is the honest position - a vendor whose accelerator record lists an interconnect with no rate cannot be evaluated for TP, and asserting a plausible number for a 7 nm Chinese GPGPU from 2023 would be exactly the invention this repo's contract forbids. ALSO WORTH RECORDING ABOUT THE SOURCE BASE: this is the same secondary-aggregator situation as huawei-hccs, which is why that record is status contested - there the aggregator at least carried a number ('HCCS 3x30 GB/s'), whereas here it carries none. MetaX's own taxonomy splits its parts across MXN (inference), MXC (training/general) and MXG (graphics), which the schema cannot express, so the accelerator record is a single combined entry and its interconnect list covers both the C500 and the N100 without stating which part exposes what - a second reason not to infer a topology here. Confidence is deliberately 0.15, the lowest of any record in this slice: a low-confidence record that is honest about being empty is more useful than a filled-in guess, and the nulls are a to-do marker rather than an oversight. KIND: filed as 'other' because MetaXLink is a proprietary vendor interconnect with no entry in the schema's enum and no analogue in the named families - the same treatment as cambricon-mlu-link, huawei-hccs and huawei-ub-link.
